Hi, fellow Goats. I've decided to write this post, and share what little I know about the topic for two reasons:

a. the "makemoneyonline" subverse is a spamfest, we can do better.

b. most people I talk to don't realize how easy it is to take advantage of class action lawsuits, which means a lot of money isn't going to the people who actually deserve it.

Lawsuits are a long and arduous process. However, thanks to the internet, we don't have to be legal experts to take advantage of them. If you've ever paid for something that was defective, or falsely advertised, there's a chance someone else did as well, meaning there's also a chance a class action lawsuit was filed a long time ago. Most of the time, the manufacturer won't admit wrongdoing. Instead, they will agree to put up a large amount of money to avoid going to trail.

An unusual example of this is when Subway was sued because their "footlong" subs weren't actually 12 inches long.

In that case, a handful of claimants leading the lawsuit won $500 each.

But that's the exception, not the rule. In a lot of cases, the damages awarded will be in the millions, and put in a "pool" for anyone to claim within a certain time-frame. The maximum "estimate" you're entitled to varies depending on the settlement. Google "class action rebates", or go here to view the newest pools.

http://www.classactionrebates.com/

You'll notice each settlement falls into two categories:

a. proof required

b. proof not required.

If you are asked to provide proof, it will usually be a receipt, but can also include phone records, bank statements, photos, or something entirely different. I usually stick to "proof not required", because I tend to lose my receipts. However, please only fill out claims that you're rightfully entitled to-- otherwise, you're taking money away from the actual victims. It's a first-come, first-serve thing.

For example, CertainTeed cement siding has an open settlement pool for $104 million, and, with proof, the average check mailed is for $7000.

http://www.classactionrebates.com/settlements/certainteed/

I'm sure you can figure out the rest, but once you find a claim, be prepared to spend 5-10 minutes filling out an online form. It'll ask the usual: name, address, phone, blah blah blah. Remember, this is a legal document, which means providing false information is a crime.

Using this method, I get a check in the mail every two or three months. I think the lowest amount was $1, and I still have no idea how that happened. But then there are $100, $300, even $1000 amounts.

You won't make a living doing this, but it's fun to get a little beer money every now and then.
Class Action settlements: the only way I've found to quickly and legally make money in your underwear.
